先聽締太鼓，不要只聽大鼓。大鼓決定重量，締太鼓決定你有沒有數對拍子。: Listen to the shime-daiko first, not only the big drum. The big drum sets the weight; the shime-daiko decides whether you are counting the beat correctly.
兩者是不同時代的產物。囃子與祭典鼓樂嵌在儀式與戲劇裡，歷史很長；組太鼓是戰後才成: The two are products of different eras. Hayashi and festival drumming are set inside ritual and theatre and go back a long way; kumi-daiko is a stage form that took shape only after the war, taking the drums out of ritual and arranging sections and lighting for the concert hall.
同一顆鼓的中心與邊緣是兩個音；注意獨奏者怎麼用邊緣的短音製造句讀。: The centre and the rim of one drum are two different notes; watch how a soloist uses the short rim sounds to make punctuation.
和中國鑼鼓相比，差別在有沒有鼓師。鑼鼓由板鼓手一人下令，其他人看鼓棒，整段節奏可: Compared with Chinese luogu, the difference is whether there is a drum master. In luogu one player on the ban drum gives the orders and the others watch his sticks, and a whole stretch of rhythm can be recited from the spoken luogu jing; taiko has no such system of calls. Festival hayashi writes time into fixed rhythm patterns, and kumi-daiko on stage writes sections into a composition, held together by rehearsal and by the ji-uchi.
和西非鼓樂隊相比，差別在領奏的概念。西非的領奏鼓會在循環上打出跳脫的訊號來換段；: Compared with a West African drum ensemble, the difference is the idea of a lead drum. In West Africa the lead drum plays a signal that breaks out of the cycle in order to change section; in taiko the drums have no such lead-against-cycle relation, and pitch and timbre are what the division of roles rests on.
和韓國四物農樂相比，兩者都靠鼓聲分層、都沒有指揮，差別在領導的位置。四物農樂有一: Compared with Korean samul nori, both layer time through drum sound and both work without a conductor; the difference is where leadership sits. Samul nori has one clear leader, the small-gong player, who drives the group with gong sound, gestures and shouts while everyone else keeps their attention on him; kumi-daiko has no single leader, and time is distributed among the base rhythm of the shime-daiko, the visual signal of raised sticks and the kakegoe, each player watching what he needs to watch.
在能樂與歌舞伎的囃子裡與太鼓分工，太鼓負責較大的時間單位: Shares the work with the taiko in noh and kabuki hayashi, where the taiko takes the larger units of time
地打ち通常由締太鼓或一組較小的鼓擔任。它的作用不是伴奏，而是座標：只要地打ち還在: Ji-uchi is usually played by the shime-daiko or a group of smaller drums. Its job is not accompaniment but a coordinate: as long as the ji-uchi is there, everyone knows the beat has not slipped. Soloists vary freely in the foreground, but the length of each solo is fixed, usually counted in cycles; when the time is up the soloist closes with an agreed gesture or shout and the others move into the next section. This division, free in front and fixed behind, lets a group with no conductor each do their own work on one shared timeline.
大聲的段落是為了對比而存在的。真正維持時間的是音量不大的締太鼓；全團的整齊度取決: The loud passages exist for contrast. What actually holds time is the modest shime-daiko; the tightness of the whole group depends on it, not on the biggest drum.
太鼓團就是一群人用力敲大鼓，越大聲越好。: A taiko ensemble is a group of people hitting big drums hard, and the louder the better.
太鼓團沒有指揮，所以演奏是即興的。: A taiko ensemble has no conductor, so the playing is improvised.
太鼓團（Taiko Ensemble）— 把日本各種太鼓組成合奏的編制，從祭典行: Taiko Ensemble — a line-up that brings Japan's various taiko drums together in ensemble, from festival processions to the stage. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
太鼓沒有旋律，所以它必須用別的方式告訴演奏者「現在在哪裡」。組太鼓把時間拆成三層: Taiko has no melody, so it must tell the players where they are by other means. Kumi-daiko splits time into three layers: at the bottom a base rhythm repeated without end (ji-uchi), in the middle the phrase sections, and on top the soloist's fixed solo section.
太鼓的聲音本身也帶有時間資訊。同一顆鼓，敲正中央與敲邊緣是兩個不同的音高與音色；: The taiko's sound itself carries time information. On one drum, striking the centre and striking the rim give two different pitches and timbres; sticks struck together, the butt of a stick on the rim, the shaft pressed on the head and released — all are sound events in their own right. These techniques let one drum be both beat and signal: the centre note is a steady beat, the short rim note is punctuation, and sticks struck together announce the start of a section.
打出樂句的重心。置於鼓架，鼓面朝向演奏者: Marks the weight of the phrase. Set on a stand with the head facing the player
找「停下來再一起落下」的那個點。太鼓團的時間感幾乎都藏在這種停頓裡。: Look for the moment when the group stops and then lands together. Almost all of a taiko ensemble's sense of time hides in these pauses.
段落切換靠的是可見與可聽的雙重訊號。演奏者會喊出掛け声（kakegoe），同時把: Section changes rely on a double signal, one seen and one heard. Players shout a kakegoe while raising their sticks overhead before bringing them down. In extremely loud passages the members actually align by watching the height of the sticks and the preparation of the body, not by listening. The arrangement on stage is therefore not decoration: drums are set in an arc or a line so that everyone is at the edge of someone else's field of view; some groups borrow kabuki's mie and freeze into a pose, which looks like performance but is in fact a rest that everyone can see.
為什麼是這些鼓而不是別的？因為太鼓團的時間靠音高分層，不靠旋律。長胴的低頻讓身體: Why these drums and not others? Because the taiko ensemble's time is layered by pitch, not by melody. The low frequencies of the nagado let the body feel the beat, the high frequencies of the shime-daiko let the ear count it, and the okedo fills in the mobility needed for moving. Once the three layers are separated, members know whom to listen to even with no conductor.
看影片比聽錄音有用。鼓棒舉起的高度、身體的重心、站位的弧形，都是拍子的一部分。: Watching a video is more useful than listening to a recording. The height of the raised sticks, the weight of the body, the arc of the standing positions — all of it is part of the beat.
祭典是最主要的場合：神社例祭的神輿渡御、山車行列、地方的盆踊與豐作祈願，鼓聲跟著: Festivals are the main occasion: the procession of the portable shrine at a shrine's annual rite, the floats in a parade, local bon dances and prayers for a good harvest. The drum sound moves with the procession and with the turning points of the rite. In the theatre, the hayashi of noh and kabuki sets the taiko into a different line-up: the taiko takes the larger units of time while the kotsuzumi and ōtsuzumi handle the fine texture; the standard noh hayashi is fue, kotsuzumi, ōtsuzumi and taiko, and the taiko appears in only some pieces.
祭典的囃子又是另一套邏輯。神輿與山車上的鼓手看不到彼此，也聽不清楚對方的細節，所: Festival hayashi works on yet another logic. The drummers on the shrine and the floats cannot see each other and cannot hear each other's detail, so time has to be written into the patterns themselves: everyone plays the same fixed pattern, and sync is kept by how the patterns interlock. The hyōshigi or the gong gives a sharp reference point that drum sound cannot cover, so members far away can still line up. Here the drum is not the star of the music but a device that gets several dozen people carrying the shrine to step together.
祭典的囃子沒有「一首曲子」的概念，而是一組隨場合替換的型；組太鼓的曲目則是有作者: Festival hayashi has no notion of a piece, only a set of patterns changed to suit the occasion; kumi-daiko's repertoire consists of composed works with named authors. That difference decides how the two kinds of group rehearse: the first by memorising patterns and by unspoken understanding, the second by full score and sectional rehearsal.
組太鼓則屬於音樂廳。曲目是為舞台寫的，通常有清楚的段落：由安靜的序開始，進入以地: Kumi-daiko belongs to the concert hall. Its pieces are written for the stage and usually have clear sections: it opens with a quiet introduction, moves into a section built on ji-uchi, then several soloists come forward in turn, and it closes with the whole group in unison. Amateur groups and school clubs often play the same structure with a simplified line-up.
組太鼓是古老的日本傳統，祭典太鼓是它的簡化版。: Kumi-daiko is an ancient Japanese tradition, and festival drumming is a simplified version of it.
組太鼓沒有標準人數，從幾個人到二十人以上都有；真正固定的是每一種鼓在合奏裡的位置: Kumi-daiko has no standard number of players, from a few people to more than twenty; what is really fixed is the place of each kind of drum in the ensemble. The big drum gives weight, the small drum gives resolution in time, and the drums in between handle movement and transition.
組太鼓的曲目寫得很緊，段落長度與齊奏位置都固定。沒有指揮不代表自由，而是把指揮的: Kumi-daiko's pieces are written tightly, with section lengths and unison points fixed. Having no conductor does not mean freedom; it means the conductor's work is distributed among the ji-uchi, the kakegoe and the standing positions on stage.
給出乾淨短促的時間點，讓鼓手在密集的聲音裡仍聽得到拍子: Gives a clean, short point in time so the drummers can still hear the beat inside a dense sound
聽祭典錄音時注意鼓聲與人聲的距離感；行列中的鼓聽起來會比舞台上鬆，那不是不準，是: On a festival recording, notice the sense of distance between the drums and the voices; drums in a procession sound looser than drums on a stage, and that is not inaccuracy but the speed of walking.
還有一個容易被忽略的層次：間（ma）。段落之間常有短暫的停頓，這個停頓不是休息，: There is one more layer that is easily overlooked: ma, the interval. There are often short pauses between sections, and a pause is not a rest but the preparation for the next unison. For the whole group to land together in the same instant, everyone has to hold the same internal beat through the pause. The longer the pause, the greater the force when they land; in taiko recordings the few quiet seconds are often more tense than the loudest passage.
長胴、締、桶胴幾種太鼓被放進同一個編制，鼓聲決定一群人什麼時候踏出下一步——這是: The nagado, shime and okedo drums are put into one line-up, and the drum sound decides when a group of people takes the next step — this is the Japanese taiko ensemble. It runs on two tracks: hayashi, which supports processions and stage performance at festivals and in the theatre, and kumi-daiko, which took the drums onto the stage after the Second World War and plays a fixed repertoire. Festival hayashi and kumi-daiko use the same drums; theatre hayashi (noh, kabuki) has other instruments — kotsuzumi, ōtsuzumi, fue — which do not appear in a kumi-daiko line-up. The two give completely different answers to the question of how time should be heard.
體力也是編制的一部分。長胴太鼓的鼓面在腰部高度、手臂由側面水平或略斜向下揮擊、行: Stamina is part of the line-up too. The nagado's head sits at waist height, the arms swing horizontally or slightly downward from the side, and the stroke is long, so a single stretch of continuous striking can only last so long; the big-drum part is therefore usually shared by several players in turn, or alternated with other drums. The changes of position on stage, stepping forward to solo and then withdrawing, look like staging, but they also distribute effort so that every loud passage has someone who can sustain it.
鼓皮繃得極緊、音高最高。常維持基底節奏（地打ち），也負責把拍點切細: The head is stretched very tight and the pitch is the highest. It often keeps the base rhythm (ji-uchi) and is also responsible for dividing the beat finely
鼓與鼓之間的音高關係是相對的，不是絕對的。每個團體依自己的鼓組決定哪一顆是「高音: The pitch relation between drums is relative, not absolute. Each group decides which of its drums is the high one and which the low one, and the set of pitches changes with the group. So a taiko ensemble does not work through intervals but through timbre and position: a drum with a tighter head handles subdivision, a drum with a longer body handles sustain. Dividing the work by function rather than by note name lets groups of any size organise time with the same logic.
鼓身淺、可置於低架或手持，用於需要視覺效果與快速換位的段落: Shallow body, set on a low stand or held in the hand, used for passages that need visual effect and quick changes of position
鼓身較輕，以肩帶斜掛，可邊走邊打，用於行列或舞台移位: Lighter body, slung on a shoulder strap, can be played while walking, used for processions or for moving about the stage
